Does the stp1 mutant behave like a kinase mutant?

Bio253 HS2026 · Topic C · group mval · final report behind the A0 poster

Published

November 22, 2026

How to read this report

Every number comes from a script in scripts/ (Steps 1–12 of our workflow); each results folder has a figure_guide_mval.md that says what each figure compares. Fold changes are log2, A − B: stp_vs_anc_at_TSB = −5.4 means higher in anc, lower in stp.

1. Question and hypotheses

Stk1 (PknB, kinase) and Stp1 (phosphatase) are encoded in one stp1–stk1 transcription unit. The stp strain carries a transposon in stp1 (NE1919, codon 189 of 247) upstream of stk1, so it may also lack Stk1 (a polar effect).

  • H1 stp has reduced Stp1 and Stk1; stk has reduced Stk1.
  • H2 Some protein responses to P. aeruginosa spent medium (PASN) differ from the parent.
  • H3 Part of the stp pattern resembles stk (shared reduced-kinase component).

2. Design and data

S. aureus JE2 (anc), NE217 stk1::Tn (stk), NE1919 stp1::Tn (stp); TSB or ~15 h in 70 % TSB + 30 % cell-free, sterile-filtered PAO1 spent medium (SN, “PASN”: only secreted molecules plus partial nutrient depletion; never living P. aeruginosa). n = 3 per group. Primary analysis: 18 samples (TSB, SN); all 27 (incl. SNpulse) inform the variance. Total proteome: 2232 JE2 proteins; phosphoproteome searched twice (STY, STYH).

3. Methods

step what rule
model limma, ~ 0 + group (9 means), every contrast written as A − B no reference level can flip a sign
hit treat() (McCarthy & Smyth 2009) H0: |log2FC| ≤ 1; BH-FDR < 0.05 within contrast fixed 12 Nov, before results; no post-hoc fold-change filter
eligibility tested only with ≥ 2 of 3 observed values in every group of the contrast missing = not detected, never 0; no imputation
interaction (mutant TSB − SN) − (anc TSB − SN) > 0: SN response lower in the mutant
H3 similarity correlation of stp and stk effects, corrected for the shared anc noise method of moments, bootstrap CI
phospho ≥ 2 of 3 per group, median per-sample localisation ≥ 0.75 (Olsen et al. 2006), S/T/Y; own BH family site − protein in the same contrast, descriptive
pathways rank test + limma cameraPR (Wu & Smyth 2012); robust = both FDR < 0.05 background = proteins tested in the contrast
robustness leave-one-sample-out, alternative thresholds, genome-position scan sensitivity only

Software: R, limma (Ritchie et al. 2015), tidyverse; versions in section 10.

Hand check of one number (workflow Step 12): the Stk1 difference stp_vs_anc_at_TSB recomputed from the per-sample values, next to the model estimate.

Code 
ab <- read_abundances("total") |> keep_je2() |> filter(locus_tag == "B7H15_06355", group %in% c("stp_TSB", "anc_TSB"))
by_hand <- ab |> group_by(group) |> summarise(mean = mean(normalized_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), n = sum(!is.na(normalized_abundance)))
model <- total |> filter(locus_tag == "B7H15_06355", contrast == "stp_vs_anc_at_TSB")
kable(by_hand, digits = 2)
group mean n
anc_TSB 16.40 3
stp_TSB 10.98 3
Code 
stopifnot(abs((by_hand$mean[by_hand$group == "stp_TSB"] - by_hand$mean[by_hand$group == "anc_TSB"]) - model$diff) < 1e-8)
explain_contrast("stp_vs_anc_at_TSB")
[1] "stp_vs_anc_at_TSB: diff = log2(stp) - log2(anc), within TSB. diff > 0 means HIGHER in stp; diff < 0 means HIGHER in anc."

Mean of stp_TSB minus mean of anc_TSB = -5.42 = the model estimate (SE 0.58, FDR 0.0013): Stk1 is higher in anc, about 43-fold.

4. H1: what do the mutants lack?

Step 3 evidence table (detections TSB/SNpulse/SN of 3 each; supplied lm_impute estimates are presence/absence evidence where lod_imputed).
short_name genotype detections_TSB_SNpulse_SN samples_2plus_peptides supplied_diff_TSB_SNpulse_SN any_lod_imputed call
Stk1 stk 0/1/0 0/0/0 -2.34 / -1.66 / -2.83 TRUE supported reduction
Stk1 stp 3/2/0 1/1/0 -2.34 / -2.01 / -2.83 TRUE supported reduction
Stp1 stk 3/3/3 3/3/3 -0.17 / -0.4 / -0.17 FALSE no reduction
Stp1 stp 1/3/3 0/1/1 -4.98 / -3.07 / -1.63 FALSE supported reduction
  • Stk1: not detected in stk in TSB or SN (0/6). In stp it is ~43-fold lower in TSB (estimate above) and resting on 1–2 peptides (29–32 in anc), and not detected in SN. The site T164 of Stk1 falls with the protein (Step 9).
  • Stp1: 0–2 peptides in stp vs 9–15 in anc. The abundance values that remain are erratic, so the size of the loss cannot be estimated. Stp1 is unchanged in stk.
  • Insertion control: ErmB (transposon marker) in 18/18 mutant samples, 0/9 anc (Step 4b, separate FragPipe search incl. transposon proteins).
  • Neighbours of stp1/stk1 are unchanged (Step 4). The pattern fits a polar insertion; protein data cannot exclude reduced stability, regulation or a secondary mutation.

5. H2: altered responses to PASN

All formal interaction hits (Step 6/7) with their Step 11 stability. First strain = the mutant named first in the contrast.
contrast protein diff FDR in words leave-one-out in shifted genomic block
interaction_stk_vs_anc_at_TSB_vs_SN rbsD -5.36 1.1e-02 SN response higher in first strain 14/18 TRUE
interaction_stk_vs_anc_at_TSB_vs_SN kdpD 5.13 0.0e+00 SN response lower in first strain 14/18 TRUE
interaction_stk_vs_anc_at_TSB_vs_SN arcA -4.98 2.9e-03 SN response higher in first strain 16/18 FALSE
interaction_stk_vs_anc_at_TSB_vs_SN B7H15_14515 2.07 2.3e-03 SN response lower in first strain 18/18 FALSE
interaction_stk_vs_anc_at_TSB_vs_SN argF -2.37 9.7e-05 SN response higher in first strain 18/18 FALSE
interaction_stp_vs_anc_at_TSB_vs_SN ilvA 2.36 3.9e-02 SN response lower in first strain 9/18 FALSE
interaction_stp_vs_stk_at_TSB_vs_SN argF 1.88 1.8e-02 SN response lower in first strain 14/18 FALSE
interaction_stp_vs_stk_at_TSB_vs_SN arcA 5.36 2.8e-03 SN response lower in first strain 14/18 FALSE
interaction_stp_vs_stk_at_TSB_vs_SN B7H15_06000 -2.67 2.8e-03 SN response higher in first strain 18/18 FALSE
interaction_stp_vs_stk_at_TSB_vs_SN lipA 3.33 8.1e-06 SN response lower in first strain 18/18 FALSE

Both mutants keep most of the PASN response (r = 0.85 stk, 0.86 stp against anc). Only 5 of 1,882 (stk) and 1 of 1,931 (stp) tested proteins change their response. Raw values (Step 6) show that argF and B7H15_14515 are mainly a TSB baseline difference in stk, arcA and kdpD differ in both media, and only rbsD is mainly an SN difference. The single stp hit, ilvA, is fragile (9/18 refits) and probably shared with stk (one stk_SN replicate only). A lower threshold (1.5-fold) triples the lists but keeps the shape: stk 15 vs stp 5 (Step 11).

kdpD is not an stk-specific response. The peptide check of Step 6d shows that the whole kdp system is switched off in PASN in all three strains: only ~5 % of the KdpD peptide observations seen in TSB remain (rank 9 of 1,121 well-covered proteins, at equal sequencing depth), so each SN protein value rests on 0–3 peptides instead of 12–27. The stk-specific interaction is therefore most likely an artefact of summarising very few peptides; it also survives only 14 of 18 leave-one-out refits and lies in a genomic block that shifts in stk (section 8). The robust stk result is the arc operon (arcA + argF).

6. H3: does stp look like stk?

Similarity of the stp and stk effects (Step 7).
layer proteins observed r noise-only r noise-corrected r 95% CI split-reference r (lower bound)
baseline (TSB) 1988 0.41 0.5 0.37 0.29-0.45 0.11-0.33
response (TSB vs SN interaction) 1853 0.43 0.5 0.38 0.24-0.52 0.03-0.15

Both axes subtract the same anc means, so noise alone gives r ≈ 0.50. After removing that part, the true effects correlate moderately (0.37–0.38): clearly above 0, far below 1. Only 3 proteins are hits in both mutants (same direction). 20 (TSB) + 4 (response) proteins differ directly; 6 of the 20 lie in genomic blocks that shift as a unit (section 8). At pathway level stp shares the peptidoglycan-synthesis and cytolysis shifts of stk, not the SigB/mazEF or ATP-synthase shifts (Step 10).

Only 91–184 of 3,774 sites per contrast are measured often and localised well enough; none responds differently to PASN in a mutant. Of 62 site hits (mostly TSB vs SN), 17 follow their protein, 40 change more than their protein (Step 9; the adjusted effect is descriptive, assuming independent layers). Genotype examples: deoB T85 lower in stk (TSB, protein unchanged), pyk T537 higher in stp, Stk1 T164 lower in stp with the protein.

stp_vs_anc_at_TSB B7H15_10925 B7H15_11110 2103129 -2.079 1.060 < 0.001

Many functional terms shift in both mutants, stp as many as stk in TSB and SN; stk has more only in the response. “Stk1 broadly involved” is therefore not specific to the kinase mutant. Two genomic blocks change as a unit:

  • stk, B7H15_11470–11590 (SigB operon, mazEF, alr1, acpS, kdpCBA/DE, murF, ddl): +1.5 log2, the top window in the genome. Unrelated neighbours rising ~2-fold together fit a copy-number change in this strain; regional regulation is the alternative.
  • stp, B7H15_10910–11150, a prophage: −2.1 log2 in TSB; it also drives the most extreme windows of both interaction contrasts.

9. Answers, limitations and follow-up

answer status (Step 11)
H1 stp lacks most Stk1 (~43-fold) as well as Stp1; stk lacks Stk1 supported; polar mechanism consistent, not proven
H2 Few altered PASN responses (5 stk, 1 stp); the response is largely intact supported, small; 2 stk hits fully robust, stp hit fragile
H3 A moderate shared component (r ≈ 0.37) plus clear differences partly supported (tentative)

Limitations. n = 3 (non-significance is weak evidence of no effect); no clean deletions or complemented strains; the stp strain is a phosphatase mutant with strongly reduced kinase, not a phosphatase-only mutant; phosphosite coverage is sparse; two genomic blocks may reflect strain differences; PASN mixes secreted molecules and nutrient depletion; total-proteome run order was blocked by group (drift cannot be separated from group).

Follow-up proposal (future experiments). (1) Sequence the three strains or run qPCR on the stk block (B7H15_11465–11700) and the prophage region. (2) Measure stp1/stk1 transcripts in stp to test polarity. (3) Compare clean Δstp1 (keeping Stk1), Δstk1 and a verified double deletion with complemented strains under PASN.
